bug_semantics: devalue.parse hydrates attacker-controlled serialized values. Its ArrayBuffer branch passed value[1] to decode64 without requiring a string; decode64/asciiToBinary trusted the supplied value's length and iterated over it, so a JSON object with an attacker-chosen large length could drive disproportionate CPU work and memory growth and deny service.
flaw_origin: bbf86c2df544f3855603012b70d2be2200c7dbf3 first added ArrayBuffer and TypedArray parsing to src/parse.js, including the direct decode64(value[1]) path with no type validation. Its immediate parent lacks the ArrayBuffer hydration branch and decode64 import, making this one-parent feature commit the atomic public BIC rather than the later e46f4c8f4724e673344100790312740a65491d66 refactor.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object author and committer are both Loris Sigrist <sigrist@hasch.io>; the complete message is 'Add support for ArrayBuffers and TypedArrays' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: GitHub advisory API https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-g2pg-6438-jwpf identifies the root cause as ArrayBuffer hydration expecting base64 strings without checking that assumption, gives affected range >=5.1.0,<5.6.2 and first patched version 5.6.2, and reports withdrawn_at=null.

CVE Services record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-22775 has cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED and the CNA description independently states that versions 5.1.0 through 5.6.1 are affected by the unchecked ArrayBuffer base64 assumption and that 5.6.2 fixes it.

git show bbf86c2df544f3855603012b70d2be2200c7dbf3 -- src/parse.js shows the first addition of the decode64 import and an ArrayBuffer case assigning base64=value[1] and calling decode64(base64) without validation; the same commit also added the serialized ArrayBuffer fixture.

Direct parent-tree verification at 50af63e2b2c648f6e6ea29904a14faac25a581fc found no ArrayBuffer, TypedArray, or decode64 path in src/parse.js; git diff 50af63e2b2c648f6e6ea29904a14faac25a581fc..bbf86c2df544f3855603012b70d2be2200c7dbf3 confirms those vulnerable lines were introduced by the BIC.

At fix parent e46afa64dd2b25aa35fb905ba5d20cea63aabbf7, src/parse.js still assigns const base64=value[1] and immediately calls decode64(base64); diffing to 11755849fa0634ae294a15ec0aef2f43efcad7c4 shows the direct guard typeof base64 !== 'string' throwing 'Invalid ArrayBuffer encoding', plus a regression case for a non-string ArrayBuffer value.

Tag topology via git merge-base --is-ancestor: the BIC is not in v5.0.0 but is in v5.1.0 (293d70bb7a3312741c370c8989fff0b5525647de) and v5.6.1 (5e07a67eda945b3ac2ebac26b18863beabee7357); fix 11755849fa0634ae294a15ec0aef2f43efcad7c4 is not in v5.6.1 but is in v5.6.2 (fcf4e88275f2e2e45b9ea70ffaa5247c8f55f057).

The public fix object 11755849fa0634ae294a15ec0aef2f43efcad7c4 has parent e46afa64dd2b25aa35fb905ba5d20cea63aabbf7 and contains the exact ArrayBuffer type-check hunk; GitHub and the CVE CNA both reference https://github.com/sveltejs/devalue/commit/11755849fa0634ae294a15ec0aef2f43efcad7c4 as the fix.
reasoning: The advisory and published CVE describe a real denial-of-service condition, not a withdrawn or rejected report. The vulnerable data flow begins when parse/unflatten accepts an ArrayBuffer record whose second element comes from untrusted JSON, passes that value to decode64, and lets asciiToBinary iterate according to an unchecked length. The smallest commit that wrote this mechanism is bbf86c2df544f3855603012b70d2be2200c7dbf3: its parent lacks the entire hydration branch, and later commit e46f4c8f4724e673344100790312740a65491d66 only refactored the already-vulnerable support. The BIC is a normal one-parent commit, so there is no squash to decompose. Release ancestry matches the advisory boundary: v5.0.0 excludes the BIC, v5.1.0 through v5.6.1 include it without the fix, and v5.6.2 includes the direct validation fix. Because the complete BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, the BIC-only attribution rule yields NOT_AI regardless of AI signals elsewhere in the repository.
